annotations.text:
The thing being replaced.

Four expense types exist — Material, Parking, Toll, Hotel — plus Travel, which rides on the assignment. Parking, Toll and Hotel always have a receipt photo; Material and Travel do not. Material and Hotel carry a name the tech typed. Any of them can carry a note.

A chip shows one of those five facts.

A and B keep the big number meaning labour, as it does today, and add the expenses beneath it. They differ only in whether the expenses get a container of their own.

A groups them and can be read at a glance from its header subtotal. B adds no furniture but needs an icon per type, and on the five-expense job its rows run into the four above them.

C is the real statement: the headline is what the job paid, the strip itemises it, labour included.

It is the only one that changes what a number already on screen means — and the week's Earned card would have to follow. Worth it if you want Pay to read as a payslip rather than an hours log.
